items.text: the rain fill is drawn finer: puddle rims are clean, smooth lines instead of steps and dots
a shelf's title is never cut short: a sequence shows SEQUENCE over its name
the Founders Club says it to you: you keep Pro free, and at 100 Club members get the pre-release of Pro
under the name in the index, what Current is made for: iPhone, iPad and Mac

in the Ensemble the screen leads the room: the scene it shows, picked by hand or played by the robot or a sequence, lands on every player's screen, so everyone sees the same field and each player sees their own touch and plays their own sound; players never take the lead themselves

Ensemble: five players, one piece of water. Each laptop plays one part through its own speaker: Deep (low bubbles, a whale, the hydrophone), Surface (drops, small bubbles, lapping), Shore (gulls, a wave washing up, a lighthouse's low pulse once a bar, surf), Walker (steps on the beat, crunchy sand on the dry side and wading on the wet, splashes) and Beachcomber (a crystal goblet, a bottle blown that follows your finger, a wet finger round a glass rim, a low ringing note). Tap, drag and hold each play a sound of the part; up is higher, right is wetter
a part's link opens Current with that part and joins one room, so the parts share a tempo; the screen's link shows every player's finger on one field, in its part's color, for a projector

Ready to perform, one button in Ensemble and in Room: the paths, hints and notices go quiet, the screen stays awake and nothing reloads; on the screen it also hides every control and goes full screen, a clean picture for the projector (or open the projector window for a second display). Tap again and everything is back as it was
the water surface is drawn finer: small splashes ring round instead of in squares
six water sounds: a step on sand, wading, a splash, a lap, a wave washing up, a lighthouse's turn; and a bottle you blow for as long as you hold

rain on a dry floor now splashes as real drops: a crown of droplets thrown out in a ring that land and stay, and drops that touch run together, bead by bead, into puddles (as in Rain on Glass). The white flashes are gone
← and → turn a dial when it has focus, instead of also changing scene (Autoplay's Every dial too)

Follows and Adjust are drawers in the color editor: Follows shows its tie on its button and opens across the whole editor, both rows seen whole with nothing to scroll; Adjust holds this color's lightness, chroma and hue; the "one ground" and "one ink" buttons are gone (clear the slot on the strip)
the ground line's counts are one dial (drag round, as Autoplay's Every), so the line is short and the dice is never cut off; every bead's dots sit under it
every line in What's new says what it is (new, fix or change); some of today's did not

the mix is a bead: between Ink 1 and Ink 2 on the strip, a round bead on the thread that ties them; a tap steps grain, speed, tempo, and its dots say which. The same between the two grounds: gradient or turns. How each mixes is in the info drawer

the two grounds are one line of beads, like Autoplay's Every: Ground 1 · mix · Ground 2 · direction (a tap turns it) · hand, beats or bars · how many · the dice. By hand you choose which ground shows; with a count the gradient turns, or the grounds swap, on the tempo; the dice picks a new length and a new direction each time
a color dragged onto an empty slot (Arrows or Pattern hidden, no Ink 2, no Ground 2) now takes, and brings it back on. Every empty swatch shows the same diagonal lines (Ground 2's X is gone)
Follows, seen: free or a color by name, then how, each way a swatch already showing the color it would give, its name underneath. No more long list

for long shows: a scene with picture moves no longer adds a copy each visit; the library is written at most once a second; a stopped bytebeat costs nothing; a video or camera driving the field reuses one canvas; a recording left on stops growing after two and a half minutes, and a full browser storage now says so
